correctness.rationale: For fixed selected pair {u,v}, each edge-query cut label is the XOR of the two vertex-incidence rows r_u+r_v. Hence support S is shattered iff all 2^s binary vectors appear among pair sums. The all-one pattern forces S to have a two-vertex cover so t<=s+2 active vertices. With s=5 there are at most C(7,2)+7+1=29 distinct pair traces, less than 32; heredity rules out larger S. For s<=4 one classifies allowed small forests by the all-one cover, and enumerates each type via explicit incidence row sums, checking isolated-vertex thresholds. The formula is 1+C(n,2)z+1_{n>=5}C(C(n,2),2)z²+1_{n>=6}(16C(n,4)+30C(n,5))z³+[1_{n>=7}125C(n,5)+1_{n>=8}90C(n,6)]z⁴. Independent direct pair-shore trace enumerations verified every coefficient at n=3..7. The original proof is correct but not original as a mathematical result.
residual_risks: Independent finite checks are bounded; unrestricted assertions rest on the reconstructed combinatorial proof.
